title: Schema and security invariants
goal: Fix authority and module data ownership before moving implementations; preserve all existing identity, tenant, consistency and transaction guarantees.
context: Architecture phase A. Approximate size: M. Installer/teardown ownership changes deliberately before 1.0; existing grant, identity and audit rows retain their meaning. Task decomposition is deferred to a separate session.

consumes: The current 0.7.0 schema-2 implementation and real-driver DDL fixtures
produces: Six-table core schema and separate Audit schema/install/health/retention ownership
Qualified fresh installation, schema-1 upgrade, schema-2 adoption and published application migration behavior
boundaries: Keep all authority tenant/context columns and uniqueness rules
Preserve migration history, populated rows and same-transaction audit behavior
Disabling a module never globalizes or deletes stored grants

include: StorageSchema, HostKeyColumns, StorageHealth and existing migrations
Audit table adoption and teardown ownership
Reserved field names and persistent format fixtures
exclude: Transaction, lock or replica feature expansion

pitfalls: A retained migration filename still executes changed StorageSchema methods
hasTable alone cannot prove an adopted audit table is compatible
An adoption rollback must retain a table it did not create
Modules must not receive unrestricted authority-table mutation

validation.procedure: Compare actual DDL and constraints on every supported driver for core-only and core+Audit; exercise fresh install, populated 0.7.0/schema-2 adoption, schema-1 upgrade and published migrations; assert unchanged durable identities/rows and tenant/context/rollback invariants.
validation.expect: All cases pass with zero grant/identity/audit-row rewrites and no optional Audit table on a fresh core-only installation.

deliverables: Core-only/core+Audit DDL and populated adoption fixtures

sections.title: Exit criterion
sections.text: No unresolved data ownership or persistent-format decision remains for the redistribution. Installation and disablement cannot widen authority or discard existing data.
